get.description: Answers whether the process is alive. Unauthenticated and touches no dependency: a liveness probe that checks the database restarts a process during a database outage (Master Plan §37.4).

500.description: An unexpected error occurred; the global filter answers an RFC 7807 problem document (Master Plan §34.3).

get.description: Answers whether this instance should receive traffic. Unauthenticated and runs every registered readiness check, naming the failing class only — never a dependency, host, or credential (Master Plan §13.1).

200.description: Every registered readiness check passed; the instance should receive traffic.

500.description: An unexpected error occurred; the global filter answers an RFC 7807 problem document (Master Plan §34.3).

503.description: At least one registered readiness check failed; the instance should not receive traffic.

post.description: Accepts 1–50 mutations, oldest device_local_sequence first, and answers one outcome per mutation (APPLIED, REPLAY, REJECTED, CONTRADICTION). A batch is not atomic: one permanently rejected mutation never blocks the others (Master Plan §38.10.1, §38.10.3). Tenant and device identity come from the authenticated credential, never the body (§38.16, §9.3).

400.description: The batch is malformed: wrong shape, more than 50 mutations, a duplicate mutation_id, or a device_local_sequence that is not strictly ascending (§38.10.2).

401.description: No valid credential: an unbound session (no `did` device claim) or a revoked device is refused `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`DEVICE_REVOKED` at the device-bound sync boundary (§12.4, §38.16, §38.16.4).

403.description: The body asserted a device or organization other than the authenticated one (§38.16, §9.3).

426.description: The client local_schema_version is below the supported minimum; the device must go read-only and upgrade (CLIENT_TOO_OLD, §38.7.2, F-15).

500.description: An unexpected server fault; the whole batch should be retried (§38.10.4).

post.summary: Push a batch of offline mutations

get.description: Returns changes with server_sequence strictly greater than `after`, ordered ascending and bounded by `limit` (default 200, maximum 1000). Paging is cursor-based, never offset. The client stores `nextAfter` only after the page is applied locally, so an interrupted pull re-fetches rather than losing changes (Master Plan §38.11.2). A cursor older than the retention window is answered `rebaselineRequired` with an empty page (§38.11.1). Tenant scope comes from the authenticated credential, never the query (§38.16, §9.3).

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Exclusive lower bound: return changes with `server_sequence` strictly greater than this cursor. Omitted means "from the beginning" (0). The client stores the returned `nextAfter` only after the page is applied locally (§38.11.2).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum changes to return (§38.11.2). Defaults to 200; refused above the hard maximum of 1000.

200.description: One page of the change feed.

400.description: The cursor is malformed: `after` is not a non-negative decimal integer, `limit` is not an integer within 1–1000, or an unknown query parameter (such as an offset) was supplied (§38.11.2).

401.description: No valid credential: an unbound session (no `did` device claim) or a revoked device is refused `UNAUTHENTICATED`/`DEVICE_REVOKED` at the device-bound sync boundary (§12.4, §38.16, §38.16.4).

500.description: An unexpected server fault; the client should retry the same cursor (§38.10.4).

get.summary: Pull a page of changes since a cursor

post.description: Refuses `UNAUTHENTICATED` for an unknown account, a missing credential, or a wrong password, and `RATE_LIMITED` while a failed-attempt backoff is active. No response distinguishes the refusal causes.
post.summary: Exchange an email and password for an access and refresh token pair.

post.description: Consumes the presented refresh token and issues a successor. Presenting a token that was already rotated is treated as reuse: the entire session family is revoked and the request is refused `UNAUTHENTICATED` (§10.3). An expired token is refused `TOKEN_EXPIRED`.
post.summary: Rotate a refresh token into a fresh token pair.

post.description: Revokes the whole family, so every access token minted under it is refused immediately. An unknown token is not an error: the response is `204` either way, so logout is never a token-validity oracle.

204.description: The family is revoked (or was already unusable).

post.summary: Revoke the session family a refresh token belongs to.

get.description: Requires `Authorization: Bearer <accessToken>`. Organizations are read from the signed token, which was populated from server state at mint time. Refuses `TOKEN_STALE` when permissions changed since the token was minted, and `TOKEN_EXPIRED` past its expiry.
get.summary: The verified identity behind the bearer access token.

get.description: Resolves the membership's role grants, then its allow/deny overrides, then the structural restrictions (the Owner holds every permission; a non-owner never holds an owner-exclusive permission). A missing membership is refused ORGANIZATION_FORBIDDEN (§9.3, §11.2, §11.4).

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization the request is scoped to.

403.description: ORGANIZATION_FORBIDDEN: no membership in this organization.

get.summary: The caller's effective permissions in this organization.

post.description: Mints an RS256 JWS carrying the effective permission set, the permissions_version, and the catalog version, with a 72-hour expiry. It reuses the identity key material and a distinct audience; no device identifier is bound here (that is M2-S5). The snapshot is never logged.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization the request is scoped to.

200.description: The signed snapshot and its expiry.

403.description: ORGANIZATION_FORBIDDEN: no membership in this organization.

503.description: SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE: identity key material is not configured; the surface fails closed.

post.summary: Mint a signed authorization snapshot for the caller.

get.description: Requires `roles.manage`. The six seeded presets are materialized lazily on first touch (§11.3).

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization the request is scoped to.

get.summary: List the organization's roles and their grants.

put.description: Requires `roles.manage`. The Owner role is not editable; an unknown id and an owner-exclusive id for a non-owner role are refused VALIDATION_FAILED. Every non-owner holder is invalidated in the same transaction (§11.2, §11.4).

parameters.name: roleId
parameters.description: The role to edit.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization the request is scoped to.

put.description: Requires `users.manage`. The owner membership is refused (it holds every permission by structure); a contradiction (an id in both allow and deny) and an unknown id are refused. The user is invalidated in the same transaction (§11.4, §10.3).

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: The membership user to update.

parameters.name: organizationId
parameters.description: The organization the request is scoped to.

put.summary: Assign a membership's role and per-user overrides.

post.description: Idempotent per organization and installation id: the same keystore pair re-verifies against the stored digest and refreshes the reported metadata. A revoked installation is never re-activated (§12.2); re-installation enrolls a new installation id. A wrong credential is refused without revealing the device state.
post.summary: Register this installation on first successful authentication.

get.description: Requires `devices.view`. Lists every device registered in the organization — label, platform, versions, trust state, and the sync metadata the server maintains (§12.5). The installation credential and its stored digest are never part of any response.

post.description: Any member, with the keystore credential proving this installation (§12.4). One transaction re-proves the device row (RLS-scoped, ACTIVE, digest matching), then writes the binding onto the verified principal’s own session and answers a fresh access token minted for it — the next request carries the `did` device claim, which the device-bound sync boundary requires (§38.16.2). A session binds at most one device: naming a different device afterwards is refused, never silently relinked. No refresh token is rotated by binding.

200.description: A fresh access token for the device-bound session.

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such device in this organization.

post.summary: Bind the caller’s current session to this device.

post.description: Requires `devices.revoke`. One transaction sets the device REVOKED and revokes every session family bound to it (§12.4): refresh dies immediately, the device-bound sync boundary refuses the next batch or page, and the queued mutations are quarantined for owner decision, never discarded (§12.5). Idempotent: revoking a revoked device answers 204 again.

204.description: The device is revoked (or already was).

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such device in this organization.

get.description: Requires `audit.view`. Reads the organization’s `audit_events` — the durable business history the §32.2/§32.2A writers append — newest first, cursor-paged on the per-organization chain position. Isolation is the database policy (§8.2), not a filter: the read runs inside the trusted tenant transaction, so no caller behavior can reach another organization’s rows. The security history (`security_events`) is owner-only and deliberately not on this route.

parameters.name: eventType
parameters.description: Restrict the page to one closed audit-vocabulary event type.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Cursor: the decimal `sequence` of the last row of the previous page, from `nextAfter`. Exclusive — the page starts strictly below it (the list is newest first).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The page size (bounded).

get.description: Requires `settings.view`. Answers the complete §22.2/§22.4 typed inventory with the §38.18 `settings_version` staleness fingerprint. An organization whose settings row was never materialized receives its defaults (version 1) — never a missing answer.

put.description: A field-authorized partial update: every provided member is checked against the §22.2/§22.4 permission column inside the write transaction (owner-exclusive fields need the owner), the §38.18 `settingsVersion` body token is enforced (a stale token answers the 409 below, never a silent lost update), and the changed row, its version increment, and the audited SETTINGS_UPDATED event commit in one transaction. Refused, unauthorized, conflicting, or failing updates advance nothing.

200.description: The updated settings with the advanced settings_version.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED — an invalid value or an empty update.

403.description: PERMISSION_DENIED, ORGANIZATION_FORBIDDEN, or an owner-exclusive field held by a non-owner.

get.description: Requires `catalog.view`. Answers the live catalog in deterministic order; `search` filters the Arabic and English names case-insensitively, and `includeDeleted` is an explicit opt into the §15.1 soft-deleted rows.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: A case-insensitive substring match against the Arabic or English name.

parameters.name: includeDeleted
parameters.description: Include §15.1 soft-deleted products (default false).

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The maximum number of products to answer (1..500).

post.description: Requires `catalog.edit`. The base unit is required at factor exactly 1; the purchasing unit is optional at an exact integer factor 2..1000000. Forty-two bits of money arrive as a decimal string of minor units (§30.1) and the priced rows, the units, and the CATALOG_PRODUCT_CREATED audit event commit in one transaction.

403.description: PERMISSION_DENIED, ORGANIZATION_FORBIDDEN, or a view-only caller.

post.summary: Create a product with its §15.2 units.

get.description: Requires `catalog.view`. Every variant answers its §15.3A.2 effective price and where it came from (VARIANT, PRODUCT, or UNSET — never a fabricated zero), and `hasCost` answers false because the costing engine arrives with M4-S3 (§30.2).

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such live product here.

get.summary: One product with its units and variants.

patch.description: Requires `catalog.edit`. Every provided member changes; absent members stay; explicit null clears an optional price. The classified changes and the CATALOG_PRODUCT_UPDATED audit event commit in one transaction; an update that changes nothing audits nothing (§32.5 class A).

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such live product here.

delete.description: Requires `catalog.edit`. The §15.1 soft delete: `deleted_at` and the required reason in one transaction with the CATALOG_PRODUCT_DELETED audit event. The variants and units stay; the live catalog simply stops seeing the product.

204.description: The product left the live catalog.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED — a missing or malformed reason.

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such live product here.

delete.summary: Soft-delete a product with its recorded reason.

put.description: Requires `catalog.edit`. The whole configuration is the new truth: the base unit at factor exactly 1, the purchasing unit at its exact factor or removed. The rows and the CATALOG_UNITS_UPDATED audit event commit in one transaction.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED — an invalid unit or factor.

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such live product here.

post.description: Requires `catalog.edit`. The typed attributes are canonicalized against the closed V1 catalog; the SKU is unique per organization by a real database index — two racing writers cannot both commit one SKU, and the loser answers 409 CATALOG_SKU_DUPLICATE. The variant and its CATALOG_VARIANT_CREATED audit event commit in one transaction.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED — an invalid value or attribute shape.

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such live product here.

post.summary: Create one variant under a live product.

patch.description: Requires `catalog.edit`. Provided members change; absent members stay; an explicit null price clears the override back to §15.3A.2 inheritance; a whole replacement attribute object is accepted only when it is fully valid. A duplicate SKU answers 409 CATALOG_SKU_DUPLICATE, and the committed changes ride the CATALOG_VARIANT_UPDATED audit event in the same transaction.

400.description: VALIDATION_FAILED — an invalid value or attribute shape.

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such product or variant here.

get.description: Requires `inventory.view`. Answers the locations stock can sit in; the V1 default location is seeded deterministically on first touch (§15.4, “V1 seeds one default location”) and is exactly one per organization by a partial unique index.

Requires `inventory.view`. Answers the §15.4 derived, cacheable quantity per (variant, location) joined with the variant SKU and the product name it moves; `variantId` and `locationId` narrow the page. A variant with no recorded movement has no level row — no stock has ever been claimed.

parameters.name: variantId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one variant.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one location.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The bounded page size.

get.description: Requires `inventory.view`. Answers the §15.4 append-only quantity history, newest acceptance first by the per-organization `server_sequence`, with every §38.14.1 identity fact. A no-op read never writes anything.

parameters.name: variantId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one variant.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one location.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The bounded page size.

post.description: Requires `inventory.adjust`. The caller-generated `movementId` is the §38.14.1 identity and the whole operation’s idempotency key: an identical retry answers the stored movement with status REPLAY (§38.9.1), the same identity naming a different fact answers 409 MUTATION_CONTRADICTION (§38.9.2), and a quantity the §15.6 conditional guard cannot cover answers 409 INSUFFICIENT_STOCK with the balance untouched and no movement recorded. First acceptance answers status APPLIED; the movement, the derived level, and the audit event commit or roll back together (§32.5 class A).

404.description: NOT_FOUND — no such variant or location here.

409.description: MUTATION_CONTRADICTION, INSUFFICIENT_STOCK, INVENTORY_OPENING_BALANCE_DUPLICATE, or INVENTORY_COST_BASIS_REQUIRED (the stock has no cost basis; M4-S3).

post.summary: Record one stock movement behind the conditional guard.

get.description: Requires `catalog.cost.edit` (§11.2: the cost-price authority; §38.5: "when a cost is involved"). Answers every level’s remaining quantity, the §30.2 moving average the engine maintains, and the exact value beneath them — quantity × average, an integer product of minor units. A level with no cost basis is answered null and counted in totals, never folded in at an invented cost. No-op read.

parameters.name: variantId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one variant.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one location.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The bounded page size.

get.description: Requires `catalog.cost.edit`. Answers the §30.2 snapshot ledger — every accepted movement that records the unit cost the engine applied, newest acceptance first, so any valuation point is reconstructible from the movements themselves. Cost is not a member of the `inventory.view` faces; this is the cost-authorized face of the same append-only rows. No-op read.

parameters.name: variantId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one variant.

parameters.name: locationId
parameters.description: Restrict the answer to one location.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The bounded page size.

get.summary: The movements that carry a recorded unit cost.

info.title: My Shop API
info.description:
The My Shop point-of-sale and back-office API. The backend is the only authority for every business invariant (Master Plan §7.3).

Business traffic lives under `/api/v1` and a breaking change requires `/api/v2` (Master Plan §34.1). v1 is supported until a stated end-of-life published with its release.

Every non-probe error is an RFC 7807 `application/problem+json` document carrying a stable machine-readable `code` (Master Plan §34.3).

`/healthz` and `/readyz` are probes: unauthenticated, outside the versioned namespace, and declaring no permissions because they have none (Master Plan §37.4). Business endpoints declare their required permissions and tenant scoping here once authentication lands (M2).

field.description: The request property that failed validation.

messages.description: Every validation message applicable to the field.

type.description: RFC 7807 type. A stable URN identifying the problem class, one page per code.

status.description: RFC 7807 status. The HTTP status the code maps to.

code.description: The stable machine-readable code the client branches on. Values are API surface: never change one.

detail.description: RFC 7807 detail. A safe, user-presentable sentence; never an internal message.

traceId.description: Correlates the response with the server log line. The only internal detail a production error carries (Master Plan §13.1).

errors.description: RFC 7807 extension: field-level validation detail. Absent for non-validation errors.

status.description: Always `ok` — this response exists only to prove the process is alive.

reason.description: A short class of failure, never a diagnostic. Safe for an unauthenticated caller: a failing check reports only the failure class (Master Plan §13.1).

ready.description: Whether this instance should receive traffic: every registered check passed.

checks.description: One entry per registered check, keyed by its registered name.

mutationId.description: Client-generated UUIDv7 mutation identity (§38.8.1 `mutation_id`): time-ordered and collision-resistant. Unique with `organizationId` in the server ledger (§38.9.1), which makes every push safely repeatable (§38.9.3).

organizationId.description: Tenant scope, taken from the device binding (§38.16), never from user input (§38.8.1 `organization_id`).

deviceId.description: The installation that produced the mutation (§38.8.1 `device_id`).

actorRoleSnapshot.description: Effective permissions at the time of the mutation, for offline authorization audit (§38.8.1 `actor_role_snapshot`, §38.17).

aggregateType.description: The kind of business object the mutation addresses (§38.8.1 `aggregate_type`). Known values: SALE, SALE_PAYMENT, RETURN, CUSTOMER_COLLECTION, INVENTORY_ADJUSTMENT — an open list (§38.8.1 ends with an ellipsis), so a new aggregate type is additive.

aggregateId.description: The local identity of the business object (§38.8.1 `aggregate_id`).

operationType.description: The operation performed: CREATE, VOID, RETURN, REVERSE (§38.8.1 `operation_type`).

payload.description: The complete immutable business event (§38.8.1 `payload`, §38.24). Append-only after commit: a changed intent is a new mutation (§38.8.2), and the server never partially trusts a delta (§38.10.1).

deviceLocalSequence.description: Gap-free monotonic integer allocated inside the local transaction: the total order within the device, independent of clock (§38.8.1 `device_local_sequence`, §38.10.2).

localCreatedAt.description: Device wall clock plus a monotonic tiebreak (§38.8.1 `local_created_at`); distinct from the server’s `received_at` clock (§38.9.1).

deviceIdempotencyKey.description: The `mutation_id` duplicated into the server payload so the server idempotency key is derivable offline (§38.8.1 `device_idempotency_key`).

deviceId.description: The producing installation (§38.8.1 `device_id`), asserted by the client. The server verifies it against the authenticated device binding (§38.16) and refuses the request on a mismatch; it is never trusted as authority.

syncBatchId.description: Client-generated identity of this batch (§38.28.1 correlation): one id links the request, its per-mutation outcomes, and the server log line.

localSchemaVersion.description: The local schema version this client speaks (§38.7.2). Below the server minimum the whole request is refused CLIENT_TOO_OLD and the device goes read-only with an upgrade prompt (F-15). The field accepts any non-negative integer so that an outdated client reaches that domain refusal rather than a generic shape error; the minimum that decides it is the server constant.

mutations.description: 1–50 mutations, strictly ascending by `device_local_sequence` (§38.10.1/§38.10.2). The batch is not atomic: each mutation is applied or rejected independently (§38.10.3).

status.description: Per-mutation acknowledgement (§38.9.2): APPLIED (first sight, applied once), REPLAY (identical payload already stored, nothing applied), REJECTED (permanent business refusal, recorded with its code), CONTRADICTION (same mutation_id, different payload_hash — 409 MUTATION_CONTRADICTION, security event). One bad mutation never fails the batch (§38.10.3).

resultRef.description: The business object the mutation produced (§38.9.1 `result_ref`); APPLIED/REPLAY only.

resultHash.description: Hash of the resulting state (§38.9.1 `result_hash`); APPLIED/REPLAY only.

serverSequence.description: The per-organization acceptance order (§38.11.1 `server_sequence`), as a decimal string so a 64-bit value survives JSON without floating-point loss; APPLIED/REPLAY only.

rejectionCode.description: The stable §34.3 code when the mutation was refused: a REJECTED business code, or MUTATION_CONTRADICTION. Absent on APPLIED/REPLAY.

receivedAt.description: The server receipt clock (§38.9.1 `received_at`), distinct from the client clock (§23.1).

syncBatchId.description: Echoes the request `syncBatchId` so a client can reconcile a batch (§38.28.1).

outcomes.description: One outcome per request mutation, in request order (§38.10.1). Length always equals the number of mutations sent, including for a partial batch (§38.10.3).

serverSequence.description: The §38.11.1 per-organization server sequence as a decimal string, so a 64-bit value survives JSON without floating-point loss.

entityType.description: The §38.8.1 `aggregate_type` the change touched (§38.11.3 change sets); an open vocabulary.

entityId.description: The local identity of the changed business object (§38.11.1 `change_log.entity_id`).

mutationId.description: The originating §38.8.1 `mutation_id` when the change came from a device mutation; absent for a server-originated change. It lets the originating device reconcile its own echo instead of re-applying blind (§38.11.2 own-echo suppression).

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change (§38.11.1 `change_log.changed_at`), distinct from the client clock (§23.1).

changes.description: Changes with `server_sequence` greater than the request `after`, ascending (§38.11.2). Empty when the client is current, and empty when `rebaselineRequired` is true.

nextAfter.description: The cursor for the next pull: the last returned `server_sequence`, or the request `after` when nothing was returned. Store it only after applying this page locally (§38.11.2).

hasMore.description: True when more changes exist beyond this page. When false, the client is caught up to the sequence this page was taken at (§38.11.2).

rebaselineRequired.description: True when the client cursor is older than the §38.11.1 retention window (default 90 days, O-21). The page is deliberately empty: the plan requires a full re-baseline rather than a partial pull that would silently drop the aged-out prefix. `nextAfter` is returned unchanged.

retentionFloor.description: The first sequence still inside the retention window, present when `rebaselineRequired` is true. A client that re-baselines to this point resumes a partial pull from it.

email.description: The account mailbox address. Canonicalized (trimmed, lowercased) before lookup.

password.example: a long passphrase, never a placeholder

accessToken.description: The short-lived RS256 bearer access token (§10.3).

tokenType.description: The scheme to send the access token with.

expiresIn.description: The access token lifetime in seconds.

refreshToken.description: The opaque refresh token to present at `/api/v1/auth/refresh`.

refreshExpiresIn.description: The refresh token idle lifetime in seconds.

refreshToken.description: The opaque refresh token from the most recent login or refresh. Presenting a token that was already rotated is treated as reuse and revokes the whole session family (§10.3).
The refresh token whose session family should be revoked. An unknown token is not an error.

organizations.description: The organizations the user is a member of, read from server state, never the request.

sessionId.description: The session (refresh-token family) this token belongs to.

permissionsVersion.description: The permission generation this token was minted against (§10.3 `perms_version`).

deviceId.description: The device this session is bound to (M2-S5 §12.4), when the bind-session route has linked one. Absent on a session opened without a device binding.

permissionsVersion.description: The permissions_version of the user at mint time.

permissions.description: Effective permission ids in catalog order.

isOwner.description: True when the membership is the organization owner.

roleId.description: The role id, or null if unclassified.

roleKey.description: The role key, or null if unclassified.

permissionId.description: A permission id to grant to the role.

roleId.description: The role id, or null to unclassify.

installationId.description: The stable per-installation identifier from the platform keystore (§12.5 `installation_id`). Unique per organization: re-presenting the same pair is an idempotent re-registration, never a duplicate.

installationSecret.description: The installation credential from the platform keystore (§12.3). Stored server-side only as a SHA-256 digest.

platform.description: The platform this installation runs on (§12.1).

osVersion.description: The operating system version, as reported by the client.

label.description: The user-editable device label (§12.1). Defaults to the platform name; the owner sees it in the device list.

organizationId.description: The tenant this device belongs to.

osVersion.description: The operating system version reported at registration or sync.

status.description: The §12.2 trust state: ACTIVE or REVOKED — exactly two states in V1.

lastSeenAt.description: When the device was last seen by the server (§12.4 `lastSeenAt`).

lastAuthenticatedAt.description: When the device last completed a successful authentication or sync (§12.1 `lastAuthenticatedAt`).

lastSyncAt.description: §12.5: the last successful sync in either direction.

clientSchemaVersion.description: §12.5: the client `local_schema_version` reported at the last sync.

clientAppVersion.description: §12.5: the client app version reported at the last sync.

installationSecret.description: The installation credential from the platform keystore (§12.3). Stored server-side only as a SHA-256 digest.

accessToken.description: The fresh RS256 bearer access token, carrying the `did` device claim (§12.4).

tokenType.description: The scheme to send the access token with.

expiresIn.description: The access token lifetime in seconds.

sequence.description: The per-organization chain position (§32.5), as a decimal string.

occurredAt.description: The server-recorded time (clients never supply it).

localOccurredAt.description: The §32.2A device-local event time, when the event carries one.

actorKind.description: The §32.6 attribution class: USER, DEVICE, SYSTEM, or UNVERIFIED — never absent.

actorUserId.description: The verified user, when the actor is one.

actorDeviceId.description: A server-resolved device, when the event is device-anchored.

targetType.description: The target aggregate type, when the event targets one.

targetId.description: The target aggregate id, when the event targets one.

documentRef.description: The originating document reference, when the event carries one.

mutationId.description: The mutation that produced the event (§32.2A server rows).

deviceLocalSequence.description: The §32.2A device-local sequence, as a decimal string, when present.

payload.description: The allow-listed payload the event type defines (§32.2/§32.2A; never credentials, §32.4).

nextAfter.description: The cursor for the following page — the last served `sequence`, absent when the stream is exhausted. Pass it back as `cursor`.

key.description: The flag key from the versioned code catalog (§22.2 typed rows). An unknown key is refused, never invented.

enabled.description: The target state of the flag (§22.2).

organizationId.description: The tenant whose settings these are (derived from the verified route).

maxDiscountAmountMinor.description: The discount ceiling as a decimal string of minor units (64-bit wire money).

discountApprovalThresholdMinor.description: The discount approval gate as a decimal string of minor units, or null when no gate stands.

discountAllowedForSalesperson.description: Whether a salesperson may apply discounts (§18).

blockDiscountBelowCost.description: Whether a below-cost discount is blocked (§18).

invoiceFooter.description: The footer text on printed invoices (§22.2).

invoiceShowLogo.description: Whether invoices show the organization logo.

customerRequiredOnCreditSale.description: Whether a credit sale requires a customer record.

featureFlags.description: The §22.2 feature flags as typed row updates. Owner-exclusive; an unknown key is refused.

unitPriceMinor.description: The product-level default price in minor units, or null when unset (§15.3A.2 inheritance).

variants.description: The variants with their effective prices.

baseUnit.description: The base unit: required, factor exactly 1.

purchasingUnit.description: The purchasing unit with its exact factor, or explicit null to remove it.

baseQuantityFactor.description: The exact buying factor: how many base units one purchasing unit holds.

sku.description: The SKU — unique per organization by a real database index.

reasonNote.description: The operator’s own words, when the movement carries one.

serverSequence.description: The per-organization acceptance order the server assigned (§38.14.1).

movementId.description: The §38.14.1 movement identity: the caller-generated UUID that is the whole operation’s idempotency key. An identical retry replays; the same identity naming a different fact is refused.

cause.description: The cause this slice produces (§15.5; other causes arrive with their owning slices).

locationId.description: The location to move at; absent names the V1 default location.

quantityDelta.description: The signed, exact base-unit delta as a decimal string (POS for a receipt, NEG for an issue).

Required for OPENING_BALANCE, PURCHASE_RECEIPT, and REVALUATION (the engine never fabricates a cost); optional for a positive MANUAL_ADJUSTMENT (with it the engine folds the offered cost into the §30.3 moving average); refused for a negative one (a consumption snapshots the engine’s current average).

status.description: `APPLIED` on first acceptance, `REPLAY` when the stored answer is returned (§38.9.1).

The sum of the valued rows’ inventory value, exact minor units (§30.2’s identity).

valuedLevels.description: How many answered levels carry a basis and are folded into the total.

quantityDelta.description: The signed, exact base-unit delta as a decimal string.

MutationId.description: Client-generated UUIDv7 mutation identity (§38.8.1 `mutation_id`): time-ordered and collision-resistant. Unique with `organizationId` in the server ledger (§38.9.1), which makes every push safely repeatable (§38.9.3).

SyncState.description: Sync lifecycle of a local mutation (§38.13): LOCAL_ONLY (committed locally, not yet eligible to push), PENDING (eligible; the normal resting state of an offline sale), SYNCING (in flight), SYNCED (server acknowledged, terminal), RETRYABLE_ERROR (transient failure, scheduled retry with backoff), CONFLICT (server state differs, awaiting owner review), PERMANENT_REJECTED (server refused permanently, owner-visible, never silently dropped). There is no `isSynced` boolean (§38.13).
